messages:
maria: FYI saw a small uptick in fncall strict rejections after yesterday's rollout. Not huge but visible in the per-route chart :eyes:
kai: Can you paste the route id and an example rejection blob?
maria: route=chat.infer.v2, sample reject payload: {"error":"STRUCTURE_MISMATCH","path":"response.toolResult"} — mostly arrays where we expect object.
trent: Is this coming from a single customer or multiple?
maria: multi-tenant but concentrated on a handful of warm customers in eu-west. sampling shows ~0.6% of calls.
sam: devops-bot flagged a metric alert this morning: fncall_strict_rejects_rate > 0.5% for 15m on eu-west. Notified infra.
devops-bot: [ALERT] fncall_strict_rejects_rate=0.62% (eu-west) — investigate.
kai: Two questions: (1) are these true model outputs (i.e., non-parseable) or adapter/transformation bugs? (2) how do we want to show these in Console — as hard errors or soft-warning? :thinking_face:
maria: Most look like model-first (model returned array instead of object). Adapters tried coercion and failed validation.
trent: For visibility we should 1) sample raw payloads for rejected calls, 2) expose a new metric fncall_softfallback_rate in Console, and 3) add a suppressor flag that lets us route failures to a permissive fallback while we debug.
sam: Agreed on sampling, but watch billing/quotas if we start storing full payloads. Need retention policy and redaction.
maria: Proposed suppressor config snippet (for canary):
```yaml
fncall_validation:
  mode: strict_canary
  canary_percent: 5
  suppressor:
    fallback_route: chat.infer.v2.permissive
    sample_rejections: 1%
    redact: true
```
kai: Nice. Two UX asks for Console: a toggle to enable canary suppressor per-route, and a small table listing sampled rejection examples with anonymized payload + reason.
trent: From infra side we also need to tag suppressed flows for billing attribution so customers aren't surprised. Suggest route metadata: suppressed=true and suppression_reason=validator_strictness.
sam: Also add telemetry field suppression_policy so we can query in logs. Example log line: `fncall_reject count=3 suppressed=true suppression_policy=strict_canary sample_id=abc123`.
maria: One more gotcha: if we auto-fallback to permissive model we might mask downstream regressions. We should set an automatic escalation: if softfallback_rate exceeds 0.5% for 1h, alert SRE and revert to strict.
kai: Sounds good. Actionables: (1) infra: add sample_rejections pipeline + redaction rules (sam) (2) console: canary toggle + sample viewer (kai) (3) product: update billing attribution docs (trent) (4) ops: deploy suppressor to eu-west 5% canary (maria).
sam: I'll open a quick runbook stub for retention and redaction.
maria: I'll attach example raw and aggregated charts to the ticket.
trent: One minor UX note: show the suppressor state inline in per-route latency/cost view, not buried in toggles. Customers should see if their route is currently being permissively routed.
kai: +1. Also plan a 7-day canary with daily rollups. If metrics stable, we can increase.
maria: Cool. I'll spin up the canary tomorrow and post results. Thanks all :party_parrot:
devops-bot: [DEPLOY] fncall-suppressor:v0.9 scheduled to eu-west canary at 2026-03-22T09:00:00Z by maria
